scope: src/companion/{client,protocol,relay}.js, src/weaponViewmodelLoader.js, src/assetManifest.js, src/data/weapons.js, src/reloadTimelines.js, src/duelArena.js, src/aaaPresence.js — cross-referenced against src/main.js, vite.config.js, companion.html

findings.title: Authored M4 viewmodel GLBs (~7.6MB) are loaded every session but can never be shown
findings.description: _loadAuthoredM4Viewmodels() runs unconditionally at module init (main.js:19506). It fetches/parses/clones/validates weapon.rifle (public/assets/weapons/m4/m4_viewmodel.glb, 6.4MB) and viewmodel.operative.hands (operative_hands.glb, 1.2MB) and parents them (invisible) to gunGrp. But every use is gated by _isAuthoredM4RuntimeActive(), which requires isPlayableWeaponIdx(0) AND P.weaponIdx===0. In src/data/weapons.js WEAPONS[0] (M4A1) is {playable:false, removed:true}, so PLAYABLE_WEAPON_INDICES = [1..7] and isPlayableWeaponIdx(0) is permanently false. The authored M4 runtime therefore can never activate; the GLB load, GLTF parse, SkeletonUtils clone, validation, scaling and GPU upload are pure waste on every load. Consistent with the project's 'GLB paths disabled by design' rule, but the disable is done at the weapon-data layer while the loader still pays the full cost.
findings.evidence: main.js:18808 `return !!(isPlayableWeaponIdx(0)&&m4AuthoredWeapon&&m4AuthoredWeapon.ok&&...&&P&&P.weaponIdx===0&&!(G&&G.splitScreenActive))` ; weapons.js:3 `{name:'M4A1',...,playable:false,removed:true,...}` ; main.js:19506 `_loadAuthoredM4Viewmodels();` (unconditional). Verified at runtime: isPlayableWeaponIdx(0) === false, START_WEAPON_IDX === 1.
findings.fix: Guard the loader: wrap the call site `_loadAuthoredM4Viewmodels();` (main.js:19506) in `if (isPlayableWeaponIdx(0)) _loadAuthoredM4Viewmodels();` so the 7.6MB fetch/parse is skipped while M4A1 stays removed. Do NOT flip M4A1's removed/playable flags (that would revive a disabled GLB path per the hard rules). This only short-circuits dead work; runtime visuals are unchanged because the rig is already never shown.
findings.risk: Very low. The branch never produces visible output today; skipping it cannot change in-game visuals. Must keep the GLB available on disk so asset probes (validate:weapons, asset-registry-probe) still pass — they load by manifest id directly, not via this function, so they are unaffected.

findings.title: Drone fire/up/down buttons never clear on pointercancel — drone can fire or climb forever
findings.description: fire-btn, up-btn and down-btn set state.sticks.fireHeld / state.sticks.ascend on 'pointerdown' and only clear them on their own 'pointerup'. There is no 'pointercancel' (or pointerleave/blur/visibilitychange) handler, and no setPointerCapture. On touch devices a pointercancel (system gesture, scroll, OS interruption, app backgrounding) fires no pointerup, so fireHeld stays true / ascend stays ±1. The 34ms DRONE_INPUT loop (client.js:788-795) then keeps streaming {fireHeld:true,ascend:1} to the host, and host tickCompanionDrone (main.js:22216 `if(d.input.fireHeld)companionDroneFire();`) keeps firing every frame until the next button interaction. Note installStick() (client.js:681-682) correctly handles BOTH pointerup and pointercancel — these three buttons were missed.
findings.evidence: client.js:745-749 `el('fire-btn').addEventListener('pointerdown',()=>{state.sticks.fireHeld=true;send(DRONE_FIRE,{held:true});}); el('fire-btn').addEventListener('pointerup',()=>{state.sticks.fireHeld=false;});` — no pointercancel. Same pattern for up-btn (750-751) and down-btn (752-753). Compare installStick which does both: client.js:681 `pad.addEventListener('pointerup', reset)` and 682 `pad.addEventListener('pointercancel', reset)`.
findings.fix: For fire-btn add `el('fire-btn').addEventListener('pointercancel',()=>{state.sticks.fireHeld=false;});` and likewise add pointercancel handlers to up-btn and down-btn that set ascend=0. Optionally also reset all three on window 'blur'/'visibilitychange' (document.hidden) to clear held state when the companion tab loses focus. Cheap, isolated to the companion client.
findings.risk: Very low. Adds release handlers only; no change to host or game logic. Companion is an optional secondary-device feature so blast radius is small.

findings.title: Duel arena declares floorY:WT but standard levels use floorY:0 (default) — possible foot/floor clip
findings.description: buildDuelArena sets floorRegions=[{...,floorY:WT}] (WT=0.4) and positions the floor mesh at y=WT+h/2-0.02 (top surface ~WT+0.33=0.73). Standard buildLevel() does NOT add a whole-room floorRegion, so _floorYAt() returns its default 0 for the room while the standard floor box (main.js:2800 `box(0,WT/2,0,RW,WT,RD,fM)`) has its top at WT=0.4. The duel arena thus uses a DIFFERENT ground-height convention than every campaign level: standard rooms drive player ground Y to 0, duel drives it to WT. Depending on how P.pos.y maps to feet, this can leave the player's feet/shadow offset relative to the visible duel floor (sinking into it or hovering). Players spawn at y=0.2 then snap to floorY=WT.
findings.evidence: duelArena.js:11 `const floorRegions=[{x0:-40,x1:40,z0:-40,z1:40,floorY:WT}];` and duelArena.js:21-22 `floor.position.set(0, WT + h / 2 - 0.02, 0)` with h=0.35. Standard convention: cover-graph floorYAt returns 0 when no region matches; buildLevel adds no room-wide region; main.js:2800 floor box top = WT.
findings.fix: Make the duel arena follow the campaign convention: either set floorRegions floorY to 0 (matching default rooms) and position the floor mesh so its top sits at y=0 like standard floors, OR confirm by playtest that WT is intended here. Lowest-risk surgical option: change `floorY: WT` to `floorY: 0` and set the floor mesh top to 0 (floor.position.set(0, -h/2-0.02, 0)) to mirror the standard sub-floor box, then verify spawns (y is re-derived from floorY by physics anyway).
findings.risk: Medium-uncertain: duel mode was presumably tested as-is, so the WT convention may be deliberate. Confirm with a quick playtest before changing — wrong direction would push the player through the floor. Only affects PvP duel mode.

findings.title: validateWeaponViewmodel hardcodes rifle-specific required nodes, ignoring entry.mechanicalParts/type
findings.description: validateWeaponViewmodel() always enforces requiredNodes=['WeaponRoot','visual','sockets','mag','trigger','chargingHandle'] regardless of weapon type, even though it accepts an `entry` with type/mechanicalParts and the manifest declares per-weapon mechanicalParts (e.g. weapon.knife=['blade'] with no trigger/mag/chargingHandle, weapon.shotgun=['trigger','pump','shell','ejectionPort'] with no chargingHandle). Any future authored knife/grenade/shotgun GLB validated through this path would always fail on mag/trigger/chargingHandle. Currently latent: main.js only ever calls validateWeaponViewmodel for weapon.rifle (the M4), for which the list is correct.
findings.evidence: weaponViewmodelLoader.js:150 `const requiredNodes = ['WeaponRoot', 'visual', 'sockets', 'mag', 'trigger', 'chargingHandle'];` then :153 `for (const name of requiredNodes) if (!nodes.has(name)) errors.push(...)`. The function signature takes `entry` (with entry.mechanicalParts) but never uses it for requiredNodes. Sole caller: main.js:19445 for weapon.rifle only.
findings.fix: Derive requiredNodes from the entry when present: `const requiredNodes = options.requiredNodes || ['WeaponRoot','visual','sockets', ...(entry.mechanicalParts || ['mag','trigger','chargingHandle'])];` (or split into structural nodes WeaponRoot/visual/sockets plus entry.mechanicalParts). Keeps current M4 behavior identical while making the validator type-correct for future authored weapons.
findings.risk: Low. Only path in use today is the rifle, which already supplies trigger/mag/chargingHandle, so M4 validation result is unchanged. Touches a pure validation helper, no render path.

findings.title: WEAPONS fields recoilZ, breathHold, adsTimeMul are defined but never read
findings.description: Several per-weapon tuning fields look load-bearing but are never consumed: recoilZ (all weapons) has zero readers in src/; recoilX is read ONLY to compute a cosmetic HUD label (main.js:32513 recoilLabel), not actual recoil — recoil is driven by shX/shY. breathHold:.4 on the AWM (idx 7) is never read as W.breathHold (the breathHold matches in main.js are an unrelated local 'knife-pair-tension' variable). adsTimeMul:.85 on the P226 (idx 6) has zero readers anywhere. These give a false impression that tuning these numbers changes feel.
findings.evidence: grep over src/ (excluding weapons.js): `recoilZ` -> 0 hits; `recoilX` -> only main.js:32513 `const recoilLabel=w.recoilX>=.10?'HIGH':...`; `adsTimeMul` -> only the weapons.js definition; W.breathHold -> 0 hits (main.js:13451+ use a local `breathHold` from knife tension, not the weapon field).
findings.fix: Either delete the unused fields (recoilZ everywhere, breathHold on AWM, adsTimeMul on P226) to remove the false tuning surface, OR wire them: e.g. multiply ADS lerp duration by W.adsTimeMul where ADS speed is computed, fold recoilZ into the per-shot camera/gun roll, and apply W.breathHold to sniper hold-breath steadiness. No-op-cleanup is the lowest risk.
findings.risk: Very low if deleting (fields are unread, so nothing changes at runtime). Save compat unaffected (these are static defaults, not persisted). If wiring them instead, that changes feel and needs tuning.

findings.title: COMPANION_PONG and HOST_DRONE_FRAME protocol constants are never used
findings.description: COMPANION_MESSAGES.COMPANION_PONG ('companion:pong', protocol.js:14) and COMPANION_MESSAGES.HOST_DRONE_FRAME ('host:droneFrame', protocol.js:7) are declared but referenced nowhere in client.js, relay.js or main.js. Ping/pong is implemented entirely via RELAY_PING/RELAY_PONG, and drone video frames are sent as raw binary (ArrayBuffer) through the relay's binary forwarding, never as a HOST_DRONE_FRAME message. Additionally the relay emits RELAY_ERROR (relay.js:156,183) but neither client.js onMessage nor main.js _companionOnMessage handle it, so relay errors are silently dropped on both ends.
findings.evidence: grep `COMPANION_MESSAGES.COMPANION_PONG` -> 0 hits; `COMPANION_MESSAGES.HOST_DRONE_FRAME` -> 0 hits across src/. Drone frame path: main.js:22285-22288 sends `blob.arrayBuffer().then(buf=>_companionSendBinary(buf))`; relay.js:173-178 forwards binary host->companion; client.js:455-457 decodes ArrayBuffer as image/webp. RELAY_ERROR handled by neither client.js (no branch in onMessage 454-493) nor main.js (_companionHandleCommand default:break, 21865).
findings.fix: Remove the two unused constants (COMPANION_PONG, HOST_DRONE_FRAME) from COMPANION_MESSAGES to keep the protocol honest, OR, if you want diagnostics, add a client.js onMessage branch for RELAY_ERROR that surfaces msg.reason in the status pill (setStatus('error', msg.reason)). Pure cleanup; no runtime behavior depends on either constant.
findings.risk: Very low. Constants are unreferenced; removing them cannot affect runtime. Adding a RELAY_ERROR handler is additive and isolated to the companion client.

findings.title: Muzzle-spill color branch for weaponIdx===0 (M4) is unreachable
findings.description: spawnAaaMuzzleWorldSpill picks the flash color from weaponIdx, including `wi === 0 ? 0xffe8cc`. weaponIdx 0 is the removed M4A1 (weapons.js: playable:false, removed:true) and is never a live player weapon, so that color branch (and the `wi === 3 ? 1.15 : 1` peak boost only applies to the shotgun which is fine). Minor: the wi===0 ternary arm and its peak multiplier path are dead.
findings.evidence: aaaPresence.js:17-18 `const col = wi === 3 ? 0xffaa66 : wi === 7 ? 0xffddcc : wi === 0 ? 0xffe8cc : 0xffcc88;` Caller main.js:26225 passes `weaponIdx:pl.weaponIdx`; player weaponIdx is always in PLAYABLE_WEAPON_INDICES = [1..7], never 0.
findings.fix: Drop the `wi === 0 ? 0xffe8cc :` arm (fold into the default), or, if a warmer rifle-style flash is wanted for the MK14 marksman (idx 5) / DMR, retarget the color to a live index. Cosmetic-only cleanup.
findings.risk: Very low. The branch never executes today; removing it does not change any visible flash color.

findings.title: Muzzle world-spill PointLights bypass the documented world-point-light budget locks
findings.description: spawnAaaMuzzleWorldSpill adds real THREE.PointLight objects directly to the scene each shot (peak intensity 2.2-3.1, range 3.4), lifetime 0.055-0.09s. With auto fire (e.g. MP9 ~13 shots/s) up to ~2 of these overlap. assetManifest.js CORE_VISUAL_BUDGET_LOCKS.low caps budgetedWorldPointLights at 3 and visibleScenePointLights at 6; these transient spill lights are not counted by computeVisualBudgetHeadroom, so on 'low' quality they can transiently push the real visible point-light count past the documented lock during sustained fire. Low impact due to the very short lifetime, but it is a quiet contradiction with the stated budget.
findings.evidence: aaaPresence.js:23 `const L = new THREE.PointLight(col, peak, 3.4, 2.05); ... scene.add(L);` ; assetManifest.js:618-623 `CORE_VISUAL_BUDGET_LOCKS.low = { budgetedWorldPointLights: 3, visibleScenePointLights: 6, ... }`. computeVisualBudgetHeadroom (assetManifest.js:662) only reads counts.budgetedWorldPointLights/visibleScenePointLights passed in by main.js, which do not include these spill lights.
findings.fix: On 'low' (and optionally 'medium') quality, cap the number of concurrent spill lights (early-return in spawnAaaMuzzleWorldSpill if _muzzleSpills.length >= N, e.g. N=1 on low / 2 on medium), and/or scale peak by the quality tier so the documented locks hold during sustained fire. Already self-expiring, so this is a tightening, not a correctness fix.
findings.risk: Very low and visible-positive on weak GPUs (fewer light recompiles); change is local to one module. Verify the muzzle flash still reads on high/ultra (leave those uncapped).
